searchText: Quick check: Does the current SELFDESTRUCT EIP mean that SELFDESTRUCT can no longer "burn" ETH in the sense of literally removing it from circulation? ooh taking a quick look, it seems like it's still possible to use it to burn ideally we would find a way to remove this option; maintain a hard "execution layer does not just destroy eth" invariant What benefit does this bring? You can "provably" still burn ETH by sending to a chosen address (e.g., address 0). having more invariants is good, by default eg. having an easy-to-instrument way to compute the "current total ETH supply" would be nice you can obviously do that now if you jerry-rig the execution client, but if we get rid of the selfdestruct burn then you would only need to jerry-rig the consensus client The amount of error produced by self destructed ETH is insignificant compared to the amount of error introduced by sending to address `0`, `0xdead...` and such. All change creates risk, and this one doesn't appear to add value that offsets that risk.
